rows.grounds: compound indicating a single unit or part; taken as the increment of measure
compound of vedikā (altar/platform) and māna (measure); object of the stated gradation
ablative used adverbially to indicate sequential progression
compound listing the three grades in descending order, qualifying the measure

items.question: By what incremental gradation is the altar's measure assigned to superior, middle, and inferior grades?
premises: The altar's measure is specified as increasing by one part.
This increase proceeds in a sequential order.
The sequence corresponds to superior, middle, and inferior grades.
items.inference: The altar's measure is graded by successive one-part increments according to the superior, middle, and inferior classifications.
uncertainties: The exact base measure to which the one-part increment is added is supplied by the preceding verses.
items.plain_english: In order, the altar's measure increases by one part for the best, middle, and lowest grades.
